headline_marked: Salman Shah murder case: [[Accused 'Don' arrested]] at Dhaka airport
headline: Salman Shah murder case: Accused 'Don' arrested at Dhaka airport
summary: Mohammad Ashraful Haque, known as Don, was detained by immigration police while attempting to travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah.
details: Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka today.
Ashraful was detained around 6:00 am as he attempted to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
The arrest followed a requisition from the CID and a court directive to prevent the accused, named in the first information report (FIR), from leaving the country.
Following the arrest, Ashraful was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further legal proceedings.
The murder case was originally filed with the Ramna Police Station in Dhaka.
The victim, Shahriar Chowdhury Emon, known by his screen name Salman Shah, was a highly popular actor in the 1990s.
Salman Shah was found dead at his Eskaton Road residence in Dhaka on September 6, 1996, at the age of 25.
caption:
A major breakthrough in a decades-old cold case: an accused in the murder of legendary actor Salman Shah has been arrested at the airport.

Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka today.

Ashraful was detained around 6:00 am as he attempted to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.

The arrest followed a requisition from the CID and a court directive to prevent the accused, named in the first information report (FIR), from leaving the country.

Following the arrest, Ashraful was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further legal proceedings.

The murder case was originally filed with the Ramna Police Station in Dhaka.

The victim, Shahriar Chowdhury Emon, known by his screen name Salman Shah, was a highly popular actor in the 1990s.

Salman Shah was found dead at his Eskaton Road residence in Dhaka on September 6, 1996, at the age of 25.

Source: Jamuna TV, The Daily Star

headline: 873 children dead from measles and measles-like symptoms across Bangladesh
summary: Six more children died in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 873 since March 15.
details: Six children died within the last 24 hours due to measles-like symptoms, according to a report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Since March 15, a total of 873 children have died nationwide, comprising 775 deaths linked to measles-like symptoms and 98 confirmed measles deaths.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,063 children were affected, with 75 confirmed cases of measles and 988 patients with measles-like symptoms.
Hospitalization rates remain high, with 938 children admitted to hospitals in the last 24 hours, and 942 children discharged.
Overall, since March 15, there have been 136,320 suspected cases of measles measles-like symptoms and 17,115 confirmed cases.
Out of the total suspected cases, 118,382 patients were hospitalized, with 114,142 having been discharged.
caption:
873 children have died since March 15 as a measles outbreak grips Bangladesh.

Six children died within the last 24 hours due to measles-like symptoms, according to a report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Since March 15, a total of 873 children have died nationwide, comprising 775 deaths linked to measles-like symptoms and 98 confirmed measles deaths.

In the last 24 hours alone, 1,063 children were affected, with 75 confirmed cases of measles and 988 patients with measles-like symptoms.

Hospitalization rates remain high, with 938 children admitted to hospitals in the last 24 hours, and 942 children discharged.

Overall, since March 15, there have been 136,320 suspected cases of measles measles-like symptoms and 17,115 confirmed cases.

Out of the total suspected cases, 118,382 patients were hospitalized, with 114,142 having been discharged.
